name: Piltdown Man — forty years of a fake ancestor
scope: The keystone forgery, and the chemistry that ended it. T1: in 1912 a gravel pit at Piltdown in Sussex produced 'the earliest Englishman' — a skull with a modern-sized human braincase joined to an ape's jaw — presented to the Geological Society of London on 18 December 1912 and named Eoanthropus dawsoni, 'Dawson's dawn man', after the amateur solicitor-antiquarian who brought it in, Charles Dawson (the hook: British textbooks taught this creature for forty years and it never existed). T2: why the experts swallowed it — it arrived exactly where national pride wanted it (Germany had Neanderthals, France had Cro-Magnon, England had nothing) and it matched the reigning theory that the big brain evolved FIRST and the ape jaw lingered behind. T2b: the doubters were on the record the whole time — David Waterston said in 1913 the cranium and jaw simply did not belong together, and the German anatomist Franz Weidenreich stated in the 1920s that the jaw was an orangutan's; being right was not enough to beat prestige. T3: the cost of the error — when Raymond Dart described the Taung Child (Australopithecus africanus), a SMALL-brained upright ancestor from South Africa, in Nature in February 1925, the British establishment brushed it aside because it contradicted Piltdown; the search for human origins stayed pointed at Europe for a generation. T3b: the forgers kept going — a carved bone implement dug up in 1914 was so oddly shaped that it was nicknamed 'the cricket bat', and a second site, Piltdown II, produced more fragments in 1915; the finds stopped completely after Dawson died in August 1916. T4: THE CATCH, PART ONE — a clock, not an argument: Kenneth Oakley's fluorine test (buried bone slowly absorbs fluorine from groundwater, so bones lying together for the same time should hold the same amount). Tested in 1949, the Piltdown pieces held far too little fluorine for half-million-year-old fossils; in 1953 Oakley with Joseph Weiner and Wilfrid Le Gros Clark added nitrogen tests, and the jaw still held the protein levels of a modern bone. T4b: THE CATCH, PART TWO — a microscope: the molars' flat 'human' chewing wear had been produced by FILING, with scratches running in directions no chewing makes, and the bones had been stained with iron salts and potassium dichromate to match the gravel. The verdict was published in Nature on 21 November 1953. T5: what the thing actually was — a human skull only a few centuries old, plus the lower jaw of an orangutan, with Piltdown gravel and putty packed into the emptied tooth sockets (revealed by micro-CT scanning in 2016). T5b: whodunnit, answered by DNA — a 2016 study in Royal Society Open Science sequenced the Piltdown I canine and a Piltdown II molar and found they came from the SAME orangutan, from Sarawak in Borneo: one forger working from one limited supply, which points hard at Dawson, a man with a documented history of faked antiquities. T5c: the echo — it can still happen and now gets caught faster: in 1999 National Geographic announced 'Archaeoraptor', a feathered dinosaur-bird from China, and within months CT scanning and the discovery of the matching counter-slab showed it was two different fossils glued together (verify details at build).
source: Grokipedia 'Piltdown Man' (primary source, read in full, accessed 2026-08-11); primary references named therein to be pulled at build: Weiner, Oakley & Le Gros Clark, Nature, 21 November 1953; De Groote et al., 'New genetic and morphological evidence suggests a single hoaxer created Piltdown Man', Royal Society Open Science, 2016; Dart, Nature, 7 February 1925 (Taung). Archaeoraptor rung flagged for independent verification (National Geographic, November 1999; Rowe et al. CT analysis).
framing_note: KEYSTONE ladder for the strand and the model 'how it was caught' arc: a chemical test and a microscope beat forty years of authority. ACCURACY RAIL (the one that gets botched everywhere): the CRANIUM was human and the JAW was orangutan — never write 'an ape skull'; and the fluorine test is RELATIVE dating (it compares bones buried at the same site), not an absolute age — teach that before testing it. Second rail: nobody ever confessed; the case was made by chemistry, DNA and tool-marks. Dinner-test payoff: the T5 orangutan-jaw-plus-few-centuries-old-skull reveal, and T4b's filed teeth. DISTRACTOR MINE: real rival hominin fossils that were genuine (Neanderthal, Java Man/Homo erectus, Peking Man, the Taung Child) and real dating methods (radiocarbon, potassium-argon, tree rings, nitrogen content) — every option a real thing a real scientist would name. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let a stem say 'the jaw came from an orangutan' and then ask what the 1953 tests showed; describe the SCENE (two bones, one pit, different amounts of fluorine) and let the answer be recalled. LANE (intra-science): the life/evolution-evidence strand owns Taung, australopithecines and human origins proper — here Taung appears only as Piltdown's casualty; do not tour human evolution in this ladder.

name: Cold fusion 1989 — the claim that replication ate in six weeks
scope: The strand's CONTROL CASE: the same machinery that catches a liar catches an honest mistake, and it does not need to know which it is. T1: on 23 March 1989 two electrochemists, Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons, announced nuclear fusion at room temperature in a jar of water — at a PRESS CONFERENCE at the University of Utah, before any other scientist had seen the data (the hook: the announcement skipped the step where somebody checks). T2: the apparatus a kid can picture — a palladium rod and a platinum wire dipped in heavy water (deuterium oxide) with current running through; deuterium soaked into the palladium metal, and their calorimeter said more heat was coming out than electricity was going in. T3: the objection physicists raised in the first week, and the best rung in the ladder — if that heat were really fusion, the cell would have been pouring out something like a trillion neutrons per second per watt, a dose that would have killed the two men standing beside it. They were standing there, unharmed. Their own survival was evidence against them. T4: the sharp reader — Richard Petrasso's plasma-fusion group at MIT looked at the published gamma-ray spectrum and found a peak with NO Compton edge, which a real gamma peak from that kind of detector must have; the claimed nuclear fingerprint was the wrong SHAPE (the reported peak energy was also wrong for neutron capture on hydrogen, 2.2245 MeV — verify at build). Their critique ran in Nature in 1989. T4b: what replication actually looked like — more than a hundred laboratories on four continents dropped what they were doing and tried it within weeks; some reported early positives, and those faded as the measurements got more careful. That is not a failure of science, that is the immune system working at speed. T5: the verdict — Caltech's Nathan Lewis and the MIT groups found nothing above background; at the American Physical Society meeting in Baltimore on 1 May 1989 eight of the nine leading speakers said the claim was dead; a US Department of Energy panel in November 1989, and a second panel in 2004, found no convincing evidence of a nuclear source. T5b: THE HONEST RAIL, stated out loud — Fleischmann and Pons were never found to have faked anything. This was error plus a premature announcement, not fraud, and the point is that the check does not care. T5c: the honest caveat the bank will not hide — a small research community still reports unexplained excess heat under the name LENR and still publishes; the mainstream position is that no nuclear mechanism has been demonstrated. The bank says exactly that and does not pretend the file is sealed by decree. T5d: WHY they went to the press — a priority race with Steven Jones at Brigham Young University, who was working on a different low-energy neutron claim; racing for credit is precisely what removed the checks that would have saved them.
source: Grokipedia 'Cold fusion' (primary source, read at length, accessed 2026-08-11); Wikipedia 'Cold fusion' (targeted read: Petrasso/MIT gamma-spectrum critique, the lethal-neutron-flux argument, the 1 May 1989 APS Baltimore session, Caltech/Nathan Lewis null results, the November 1989 DOE ERAB panel, and the explicit absence of any fraud finding). Gamma peak energy figure flagged for build-time verification against Petrasso et al., Nature, 1989.
framing_note: Shape A discovery/episode ladder, but it functions as the strand's METHOD spine: replication is the strand's hero and this is the case where it fires against honest people. RAIL (non-negotiable): Fleischmann and Pons were never shown to have committed fraud — never call them frauds, never let a distractor imply a confession. Second rail: do NOT write 'cold fusion is impossible'; the accurate statement is that the 1989 claim failed replication and no nuclear mechanism has been demonstrated. Dinner-test payoff: T3 — if it were fusion, the neutrons would have killed them. Second payoff: T4's gamma peak with no Compton edge (teach 'Compton edge' in context before testing it, or key the rung on 'the peak was the wrong shape'). DISTRACTOR MINE: the real chemistry and physics that could explain the heat — recombination of deuterium and oxygen inside the cell, calorimetry/stirring error, background cosmic neutrons, muon-catalysed fusion (Steven Jones's real subject), tokamak hot fusion, the Farnsworth fusor. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never state 'no neutrons were detected' in a stem that then asks why physicists disbelieved the heat.

name: Theranos — 'show me the machine working'
scope: A nine-billion-dollar claim undone by the simplest demand in science. T1: Theranos promised that one drop of blood from a finger-prick could run hundreds of tests on its own machine, the Edison — and at its peak in 2014 the company was valued at about $9 billion. What actually ran most of the tests: ordinary commercial blood analysers bought from Siemens (the hook: the revolutionary box was mostly a prop). T2: the physical impossibility underneath the story — one finger-prick drop is roughly 50-100 microlitres; split it 200 ways and each test gets less than a microlitre, below the detection limit of the chemistry involved. The claim broke analytical chemistry before it ever broke the law. T3: so Theranos DILUTED the tiny sample with fluid to make up the volume the commercial machines needed — which drags the thing you are measuring down toward the noise and multiplies the error, disastrously so for tightly-ranged results like potassium. T3b: the number that made it real — internal quality-control records showed the Edison failing its own accuracy check for testosterone about 87% of the time in February 2015 (verify at build), and in May 2016 Theranos voided roughly two years of results it had already given to real patients. T4: WHO CAUGHT IT — not a regulator, not the board, not an investor: two young lab employees, Erika Cheung and Tyler Shultz (grandson of board member George Shultz), who watched the quality-control failures from inside the lab. Cheung wrote to the federal lab regulator CMS; Shultz went to the New York State health department and then to Wall Street Journal reporter John Carreyrou, whose first article ran on 15 October 2015. T4b: the inspection that followed — CMS examined the Newark, California lab and concluded in a January 2016 letter that it posed 'immediate jeopardy to patient health and safety'. T5: the board that asked nothing — Henry Kissinger, George Shultz, William Perry, James Mattis, Sam Nunn, Gary Roughead: statesmen and generals, and not one clinical laboratory scientist. Prestige was seated where expertise should have been. T5b: THE ONE QUESTION nobody with money insisted on: run the test in front of me, start to finish, on this machine, right now. Demonstrations for visitors were staged. T5c: the verdict — Elizabeth Holmes convicted of four counts of wire fraud in January 2022 and sentenced in November 2022 to 11 years 3 months; Sunny Balwani convicted on all twelve counts in July 2022.
source: Grokipedia 'Theranos' (primary source, read at length, accessed 2026-08-11 — Edison claims, the modified Siemens analysers and Tecan dilution, the February 2015 testosterone QC failure rate, the ~2 years of voided results, board composition, valuation and funding); Wikipedia 'Theranos' and 'Elizabeth Holmes' (Carreyrou's October 2015 WSJ investigation, the January 2016 CMS 'immediate jeopardy' finding, convictions and sentences). Erika Cheung's CMS complaint and Tyler Shultz's route to the New York State health department flagged for build-time citation.
framing_note: Shape A ladder; the strand's TEST-IT-YOURSELF payoff, because the catch was a demand a child can make: show me it working. RAIL: the Edison existed and did run some tests — the fraud was claiming it ran all of them; write 'modified commercial analysers made by Siemens', never 'they had no machines at all'. Second rail: lab-on-a-chip microfluidics is a REAL and working technology for targeted single tests — do not let the ladder teach that small-sample diagnostics are fake; what failed was hundreds of assays from one drop. TONE RAIL: do not use the death of chief scientist Ian Gibbons as material. Dinner-test payoff: T1 (the machine was a Siemens box) and T4 (two junior lab staff, not the generals). DISTRACTOR MINE: real blood-testing science — venipuncture volumes, haemolysis, immunoassay, mass spectrometry, HPLC, point-of-care glucose meters (a real device that genuinely works on a drop) — and real named people in the story. No joke options. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let a stem mention Siemens before asking what actually ran the tests.

name: Wakefield 1998 — a warning that points both ways
scope: The case the bank tells in FULL, because it is a lesson about authority in two directions. T2: on 28 February 1998 The Lancet published a case series of twelve children with bowel disease and developmental regression, led by Andrew Wakefield at the Royal Free Hospital. The paper itself said it did NOT prove a link to the MMR vaccine. What set off a national panic was the PRESS CONFERENCE held alongside it, where Wakefield told reporters parents should consider three separate single vaccines instead of the combined one (the hook: the panic came from the podium, not the paper). T3: THE ANSWER WAS A TEST, NOT A RULING — the reply to a twelve-child case series was epidemiology at scale: a Danish study of 537,303 children (Madsen et al., NEJM 2002) and a later Danish study of 657,461 children (Hviid et al., Annals of Internal Medicine 2019) found no association between MMR and autism. Half a million children counted, not a consensus declared. T3b: why the coincidence felt so real to parents — regressive autism typically becomes visible in the second year of life, which is exactly when the MMR is given; two things happening in the same months is the oldest trap in causal reasoning, and it is why you need the big comparison. T4: what one reporter dug up — Brian Deer of The Sunday Times showed Wakefield had been paid by solicitor Richard Barr at £150 an hour, starting two years BEFORE publication, to help build litigation against vaccine manufacturers, with £55,000 from the Legal Aid Board; Deer documented £435,643 in total by 2006, none of it disclosed to The Lancet or its readers. Wakefield also had an interest in a patent for a rival single measles vaccine. T4b: Deer further showed the children's medical records did not match the paper's descriptions of them; the BMJ published his analysis in January 2011 under the description 'an elaborate fraud'. T4c: the chronology — ten of the co-authors retracted the paper's interpretation in March 2004; The Lancet retracted it in full in February 2010; the General Medical Council found serious professional misconduct in January 2010 and struck Wakefield off on 24 May 2010. T5: THE OTHER DIRECTION, the rung the bank refuses to skip — the senior clinician on that paper, the paediatric gastroenterologist John Walker-Smith, was struck off alongside Wakefield and then WON his appeal in the High Court in March 2012; the judge quashed the panel's findings against him and his name was restored to the register. A disciplinary tribunal is not a laboratory. It can be wrong in either direction — which is exactly why the load-bearing refutation here is the half-million-child study, not the erasure of a name. T5b: the cost — MMR uptake in the UK fell, measles returned, and children were hospitalised and died. A claim that had never survived a test was paid for by people who never made it.
source: Grokipedia 'Andrew Wakefield' (primary source, read at length, accessed 2026-08-11 — the 1998 case-series methodology, the 12 children, the explicit non-causal framing, the press conference, the ethical and financial findings, the retraction and erasure, and the honest note that gut pathology in autistic children was later corroborated independently of vaccination); Wikipedia 'Lancet MMR autism fraud' (Deer's Sunday Times and BMJ findings, payment figures, retraction chronology, GMC dates, replication studies) and Wikipedia 'John Walker-Smith' (March 2012 High Court reversal, BBC 7 March 2012). Build must pull: Madsen et al. NEJM 2002; Hviid et al. Ann Intern Med 2019; Deer, BMJ, January 2011; the 2012 Walker-Smith judgment (judge's name and exact wording — VERIFY, do not assert from memory).
framing_note: STANCE LADDER — vision_mandated. The bank's committed position here is a METHOD position, and it must be visible in the ladder's architecture: the thing that refuted Wakefield is the counted evidence, and the thing that should not be treated as proof is the tribunal. PRESENT, never preach; the word 'anti-vaxxer' is never used; no sneering at frightened parents, whose reasoning (T3b) is treated as the honest mistake it was. RAIL: the 1998 paper explicitly disclaimed proving causation — never write a stem asserting flatly that 'the paper claimed MMR causes autism'; it hypothesised, and the press conference amplified. RAIL: the Walker-Smith appeal is real, documented, and must be stated — but state it precisely (his findings were quashed; Wakefield's were not appealed successfully) and verify the judgment wording at build. Dinner-test payoff: T3 — 657,461 children. DISTRACTOR MINE: real adjacent science, all of it live — the real timing coincidence with the vaccine schedule, the real and independently replicated finding of gastrointestinal problems in autistic children, thimerosal (a separate claim studied separately), genetic and paternal-age findings in autism, the real Danish register studies. LANE (intra-science, important): the life/'Vaccines under scrutiny' strand owns the institutional vaccine story — Cutter, SV40, the schedule, NCVIA 1986, VAERS, mandates. This ladder owns ONLY the Wakefield case and the two-direction lesson about authority; do not let it drift into the schedule debate.

name: Jan Hendrik Schön — the noise that was too identical
scope: The purest catch in modern physics: a stranger with two printed graphs. T2: at Bell Labs in 2001 a young German physicist was an author on a new paper on average every eight days, and his results kept being exactly what the field most wanted — organic crystals that superconducted, and a transistor built from a single layer of dye molecules (the hook: the rate itself, one paper every eight days). T3: THE CATCH — physicists reading the published figures noticed the same NOISE. Julia Hsu and Lynn Loo spotted duplicated data in April 2002; Lydia Sohn at Princeton then saw that two experiments supposedly run at very different temperatures carried IDENTICAL noise wiggles; Paul McEuen at Cornell found the same noise again in a third paper. T4: WHY that is fatal — noise is the one thing in an experiment that can never repeat. The jitter in a measurement is thermal and random; two runs cannot share a noise trace any more than two handfuls of dice can land in the same sequence. Every real curve carries a unique fingerprint, and he had photocopied the fingerprint. T4b: the investigation — a committee chaired by Malcolm Beasley reported in September 2002 that misconduct was established in at least sixteen of twenty-four examined cases: whole datasets reused across unrelated experiments, and some 'measurements' produced from mathematical functions rather than any instrument. His roughly twenty co-authors were cleared. T5: consequences — about two dozen papers withdrawn from Science, Nature, Physical Review, Applied Physics Letters and Advanced Materials; the University of Konstanz revoked his doctorate in 2004, and after a decade of appeals Germany's Federal Constitutional Court confirmed the revocation in 2014. T5b: THE SYSTEM LESSON, stated plainly — not one peer reviewer at any of those journals caught it, because peer reviewers read manuscripts and never see raw data. It was caught by READERS who put two printed figures side by side. T5c: the honest coda — the physical claims themselves were not crazy; organic semiconductors are a real, active field, which is exactly why a field wanting a result is the most dangerous place for a fabricator to work.
source: Wikipedia 'Schön scandal' (read in detail: publication rate, Hsu and Loo's April 2002 duplication finding, Lydia Sohn's identical-noise observation, Paul McEuen's confirmation, the Beasley committee report of September 2002 and its 16-of-24 finding, the retraction count and journals, the 2004 doctorate revocation and its 2014 confirmation). Build should corroborate against the published Beasley report and Bell Labs' 2002 statements.
framing_note: Shape A, and the strand's cleanest MECHANISM rung: teach WHY identical noise is impossible before testing it. RAIL: the co-authors were formally exonerated — do not write a rung that smears them; and it was fellow physicists reading published figures, not peer review and not his employer, who caught him. Retraction count varies by source (roughly 25-28) — write 'about two dozen', not a false-precision number. Dinner-test payoff: T3/T4 — the same random wiggle in two different experiments. DISTRACTOR MINE: real physics a reader could plausibly have noticed instead — thermal (Johnson-Nyquist) noise, shot noise, a suspicious lack of error bars, impossible sample purity, superconducting transition temperatures, real organic semiconductor materials (pentacene), the real single-molecule transistor problem. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never say 'he reused data' in a stem that then asks what Sohn noticed — describe the SCENE (two papers, two temperatures, one printed page held against another) and let the answer be recalled knowledge.

name: Diederik Stapel — caught by his own students
scope: The whistle blown from below. T2: a celebrated Dutch social psychologist produced studies that always came out perfectly, and in 2011 his most publicised claim — that meat-eaters are more selfish than vegetarians — went to the Dutch press in a bulletin before any journal saw it (the hook: the press release with no paper behind it). T3: THE CATCH — three of his own junior researchers. They had noticed he always handed them finished datasets nobody had watched him collect, and discouraged questions about where they came from; when they finally compared the files, they found IDENTICAL rows of scores appearing in two supposedly different studies. T3b: the confrontation — asked where the data came from, Stapel said schools he had special access to; asked for the contacts at those schools, he admitted the schools did not exist. That admission, not any statistical test, ended it. T4: the structural tell, and the transferable lesson — one person controlled the only copy of reality. Every study ran through his hands, and nobody else ever met a participant. Any arrangement where one person is the sole source of the data is a fraud waiting to happen, however trusted that person is. T4b: what the students did next — they took it to department head Marcel Zeelenberg, who took it to the university's rector, and formal investigations opened at three universities within days. T5: the Levelt Committee's final report (28 November 2012) found fabricated or manipulated data in at least 55 publications; 58 papers were ultimately retracted, including a 2011 Science paper on disorder and stereotyping retracted that December. T5b: the human cost the bank names — graduate students had built doctorates on results that were never real, and none of them had known. T5c: the 'too good' tell — real data are noisy and messy; the committee noted the results fitted their hypotheses so neatly that the numbers themselves should have raised suspicion years earlier.
source: Wikipedia 'Diederik Stapel' (read in detail: the carnivore press bulletin, the 2011 Science 'coping with chaos' paper and its December 2011 retraction, the three junior researchers and the identical-row discovery, the nonexistent schools, Zeelenberg and Eijlander, the Levelt Committee interim report of 31 October 2011 and final report of 28 November 2012, the 55 fabricated publications and 58 retractions, the 2013 settlement and surrendered doctorate).
framing_note: Shape A. The payoff is WHO caught him — his own students, the least powerful people in the building — which is the strand's recurring shape and the one most worth a kid absorbing. RAIL: keep the fraud type straight — Stapel FABRICATED (invented numbers outright), which is a different thing from p-hacking or selective reporting; do not blur them, and do not let this ladder carry the systemic replication-crisis story. The three students are unnamed in the record — never invent names for them. Dinner-test payoff: T3b — 'the schools do not exist'. DISTRACTOR MINE: real methods and real ways fabrication actually gets spotted — duplicated rows, standard deviations that are impossible for the scale used, the GRIM test, Benford's law, failure to replicate, preregistration — plus the real social-psychology findings of the era (priming, ego depletion) as adjacent-but-wrong options. LANE (intra-science): the 'replication crisis' strand owns Ioannidis, p-hacking, publication bias and the systemic fixes; this ladder owns only the Stapel case and the students.

name: Hwang Woo-suk — the cloned-cell hero unravelled by strangers on a message board
scope: A national hero, and the one part of his work that was real. T2: in 2004 and again in 2005 South Korea's most celebrated scientist reported in Science that he had made patient-matched human embryonic stem-cell lines by cloning — eleven of them from 185 eggs in the 2005 paper. He was on a postage stamp and given a government security detail. Out of all of it, ONE result survived scrutiny: Snuppy, an Afghan hound, the first cloned dog, later confirmed genuine by the investigating panel using 27 genetic markers plus mitochondrial DNA. T3: THE CATCH, PART ONE — anonymous scientists posting on the Korean research website BRIC compared the published photographs of the supposedly different stem-cell colonies and found the SAME colony photographed twice. Ordinary readers, on a message board, with the published figures. T4: THE CATCH, PART TWO — the MBC television programme PD Note broadcast on 22 November 2005 reported that eggs had been taken from his own junior researchers and purchased from paid donors; the report was accurate and the public turned on the broadcaster, and sponsors withdrew. Then co-author Roh Sung-il said in mid-December that Hwang had admitted faking nine of the eleven lines, and DNA testing showed those nine shared identical DNA — they were not eleven patients' cells at all. T5: the Seoul National University panel reported on 10 January 2006 that ALL eleven lines were fabricated, and that his team had used at least 2,061 eggs between 2002 and 2005 — an order of magnitude beyond the number reported. T5b: the ethics failure was inseparable from the fraud — Hwang had personally handled the donation consent forms for his own junior staff, people who could not freely say no to him. T5c: the coda, told honestly — he was convicted in 2009 of embezzlement and bioethics violations and given a suspended sentence, but was cleared of the fraud charge itself; and the problem he claimed to have solved was genuinely solved by someone else, when Shinya Yamanaka showed that ordinary adult cells could be reprogrammed to pluripotency without eggs or embryos at all.
source: Wikipedia 'Hwang Woo-suk' (read in detail: the March 2004 and June 2005 Science papers, the 185-egg claim, Snuppy's confirmed authenticity via 27 markers and mtDNA, the duplicated colony photographs, the 22 November 2005 PD Note broadcast and the public backlash, Roh Sung-il's December 2005 disclosure and the identical-DNA finding, the SNU panel report of 10 January 2006, the 2,061 eggs, the 2009 conviction and 2014 Supreme Court affirmation). Yamanaka iPSC rung to be sourced at build (Takahashi & Yamanaka 2006; 2012 Nobel).
framing_note: Shape A. RAIL, and it is the one everyone gets wrong: SNUPPY WAS REAL — never write a rung implying the whole body of work was fake, and never let a distractor rest on 'the dog was faked too'. Second rail: the 2004 line may have arisen by parthenogenesis rather than cloning — if the build touches it, say 'not the cloning that was claimed', carefully. TONE: the egg-donation coercion of junior female researchers is stated plainly and once, without detail; the ladder's subject is how the claim was checked. Dinner-test payoff: T3 — the same photograph of the same cells, spotted by anonymous readers. DISTRACTOR MINE: real cloning and stem-cell science — Dolly and somatic cell nuclear transfer, induced pluripotent stem cells, parthenogenesis, adult/haematopoietic stem cells, and the real named people in the story. LANE: the ANIMAL bank owns dogs as animals — Snuppy appears here strictly as a cloning RESULT, never as dog biology or breed material.

name: Surgisphere 2020 — the database that was never there
scope: Two of the most prestigious journals in medicine, one imaginary dataset, thirteen days. T3: on 22 May 2020, in the middle of the pandemic, The Lancet published an analysis of roughly 96,000 hospitalised COVID patients from 671 hospitals across six continents concluding that hydroxychloroquine raised the risk of death; within days the World Health Organization suspended the hydroxychloroquine arm of its worldwide Solidarity trial. The data came from a company almost nobody in the field had heard of — Surgisphere, founded by Sapan Desai, with around eleven employees (the hook: a global hospital database run by fewer people than a football team). T4: THE CATCH — outside researchers read the NUMBERS instead of the conclusion. The Australian figures implied more in-hospital COVID deaths than Australia had recorded in the entire country at that point; one hospital listed as Australian was in Asia; the patient demographics and drug doses were implausibly uniform across continents that record data in completely different ways; and no epidemiologist could recall ever hearing of a live 1,200-hospital database. T4b: on 28 May 2020 more than 200 researchers and clinicians published an open letter setting out the impossibilities and asking, simply, for the data. T5: the end — Surgisphere refused to give the raw dataset to independent auditors, citing client confidentiality. With no data there was nothing to check, and the co-authors could not vouch for what they had never seen; The Lancet paper and a New England Journal of Medicine paper from the same source (published 1 May) were both retracted on 4 June 2020. T5b: what actually failed, said without preaching — peer review does not audit data; reviewers read a manuscript. Two elite journals, their referees, and a global trial policy all moved on a dataset no outsider had ever inspected, and the correction came from strangers with a calculator and a population figure. T5c: THE NO-OVERCORRECTION RUNG: showing that this paper was worthless did NOT show that hydroxychloroquine works. That question was answered separately and properly, by large randomised trials (RECOVERY, and the WHO's own Solidarity), which found no mortality benefit in hospitalised patients. A bad study being exposed tells you about the study, not about the drug.
source: Wikipedia 'Surgisphere' (read in detail: Sapan Desai, the ~11 employees, the 22 May Lancet and 1 May NEJM papers, the WHO trial suspension and resumption, the Australian data impossibility and the Asian hospital listed as Australian, the implausible uniformity, the 28 May open letter by 200+ researchers, the refusal of independent audit, and the 4 June 2020 retractions). Build must verify the exact Lancet cohort figures (96,032 patients / 671 hospitals) and pull the Guardian investigation and the RECOVERY/Solidarity hydroxychloroquine results directly.
framing_note: STANCE LADDER — vision_mandated, because it is the bank's method-versus-institution recognition skill in its cleanest form: the failure was institutional, the correction was individual. PRESENT, never preach; no sneering at the journals, the documented sequence is damning enough, and no villain voice. RAIL (the most important one in this spec): the ladder must include T5c explicitly — exposing a fake study is NOT evidence for the drug; the honest answer on hydroxychloroquine came from randomised trials and was negative for hospitalised patients. Without that rung this ladder becomes advocacy and fails the moral audit. Second rail: distinguish the two papers (NEJM 1 May, Lancet 22 May) and get the single retraction date right (4 June 2020). Dinner-test payoff: T4 — more deaths in the dataset than the country had recorded. DISTRACTOR MINE: real epidemiology a reader could have flagged instead — confounding by indication, propensity-score matching, observational versus randomised evidence, registry data, survivorship bias — plus the real journals and real trials by name. LANE (intra-science): the 'COVID, honestly' strand owns lockdowns, schools, masks, natural immunity and lab-leak; this ladder owns only the fake-database case and what peer review does not do.

name: The hoax papers — Sokal 1996 and the grievance-studies affair 2018
scope: Two deliberate nonsense papers, and an honest scoreboard of what they did and did not prove. T3: in 1996 the NYU physicist Alan Sokal published an article in the cultural-studies journal Social Text arguing that physical reality — quantum gravity specifically — is 'a social and linguistic construct'. Three weeks later he announced in the magazine Lingua Franca that he had written it as a test to see whether a journal would print flattering nonsense (the hook: the author of the paper announced it was garbage). T3b: what he had actually salted it with — real physicists' technical terms used wrongly, and claims a first-year physics student would refuse; the test was whether jargon plus agreeable politics could substitute for checking. T4: THE FAIR CAVEAT the bank insists on, and the rung that makes this ladder honest — Social Text did not operate peer review at the time and never sent the paper to a physicist. What the hoax demonstrated was a failure of EDITORIAL judgement, not a failure of peer review, and Sokal's own stated claim was narrower than the headlines it produced. T5: the sequel — between 2017 and 2018 Peter Boghossian, James Lindsay and Helen Pluckrose sent twenty fabricated papers to genuinely peer-reviewed journals. Four were published and three more accepted before the project was exposed; the published set included a study of 'rape culture' among dogs in dog parks in Gender, Place & Culture, praised by a reviewer as 'incredibly innovative', and a passage of Hitler's Mein Kampf rewritten in contemporary feminist-theory language and accepted by Affilia. T5b: WHAT ENDED IT — not a reviewer spotting the content: a journal asked for proof that the author 'Helen Wilson' was a real person, and she was not. The Wall Street Journal published the exposure on 2 October 2018. T5c: the honest scoreboard, both columns — the project had no control group, and nonsense also gets into technical journals (computer-generated SCIgen papers were withdrawn in bulk by Springer and IEEE in 2014); a hoax measures what gatekeeping catches, not whether a field's ideas are true. The bank reports the finding AND the objection and leaves the reader to weigh them.
source: Wikipedia 'Sokal affair' (Sokal's identity, 'Transgressing the Boundaries: Towards a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity', the Spring/Summer 1996 'Science Wars' issue, the Lingua Franca reveal, the confirmed absence of peer review at Social Text, and the editors' rebuttal) and Wikipedia 'Grievance studies affair' (Boghossian/Lindsay/Pluckrose, 2017-18, 20 papers: 4 published, 3 accepted, 6 rejected, 7 under review; the dog-park paper in Gender, Place & Culture; the Mein Kampf rewrite in Affilia; the WSJ exposure of 2 October 2018 triggered by the 'Helen Wilson' identity check; the control-group and ethics criticisms). SCIgen/Springer-IEEE 2014 withdrawals to be verified at build.
framing_note: STANCE-ADJACENT — vision_mandated, because it touches the bank's postmodern-frame-as-a-claim lean; the discipline required is therefore MAXIMUM. The ladder's subject is the MECHANICS of gatekeeping, not a dunk on a field: the reader should finish knowing precisely what review does and does not check. RAIL: Social Text was not peer-reviewed — say so, in the ladder, at T4; a ladder that lets a kid think 'peer review published this' is teaching a falsehood. Second rail: exact numbers on the 2018 project — 20 submitted, 4 published, 3 accepted; do not round upward. Third rail: T5c is mandatory — the control-group objection is a real methodological point and stating it is what keeps the ladder scientific rather than partisan. Dinner-test payoff: T5b — the hoax survived review and died when someone asked whether the author existed. DISTRACTOR MINE: real publishing machinery — peer review, editorial review, desk rejection, predatory/pay-to-publish journals, preprints, SCIgen, retraction — all live, none jokes. LANE: the PHILOSOPHY bank owns postmodernism and social-construction-of-truth as reasoning topics; this ladder must key the hoax mechanics and the limits of gatekeeping, never argue the philosophy.
history_overlap: philosophy bank: postmodernism / social-construction-of-knowledge ladders (and moral_vision's postmodern-frame-as-a-claim material) — this ladder must key the hoax mechanics and what editorial review does and does not check, never the philosophical critique itself.

name: The volunteer detectives — Elisabeth Bik and the duplicated image
scope: CONCEPT ladder: the modern catch mechanism, told across the cases that display it. T2: a Dutch microbiologist reading papers in her evenings can see, on a printed page, that the same photograph of the same patch of cells has been used for two different experiments. Elisabeth Bik began this work in 2013 after discovering that one of her own papers had been plagiarised; screening 20,621 published biology papers, she and her co-authors found roughly one in twenty-five contained inappropriately duplicated images (Bik, Casadevall & Fang, mBio, 2016). T3: THE MECHANISM — a western blot or a microscope field has a unique speckle and smudge pattern, effectively a fingerprint. Rotate it, mirror it, stretch it, drop it into a different figure, and the speckles still match. Fabrication that would be invisible in a table of numbers is visible in a picture, to a patient eye. T4: WHERE the checking now happens, and who pays for it — PubPeer, an open site where anyone may post comments on any published paper, and Retraction Watch, which tracks retractions across all of science. Neither is a journal, a university, or a government; the work is largely volunteer (verify founding years and founders at build: PubPeer 2012, Brandon Stell; Retraction Watch 2010, Ivan Oransky and Adam Marcus). T4b: THE BIGGEST CATCH — Vanderbilt neuroscientist Matthew Schrag examined the images behind Aβ*56, a form of amyloid protein reported in a 2006 Nature paper by Sylvain Lesné as a direct cause of memory loss. That paper had become one of the most-cited works in Alzheimer's research, with roughly 2,300 citations. Charles Piller laid out the evidence in Science in July 2022; Nature retracted the paper in June 2024, citing splicing, duplication, and use of an eraser tool. T5: THE HONEST LIMIT, and the rung that must not be cut — this did NOT overturn the amyloid hypothesis. Aβ*56 was one candidate molecule among many; Dennis Selkoe, a leading amyloid researcher, called the manipulation egregious while stating the broader hypothesis remains viable. Say exactly what the evidence shows and not one step more. T5b: another mode of catching, the oldest one — STAP cells: two Nature papers in January 2014 claimed ordinary cells could be turned into stem cells by a mild acid bath. Laboratories worldwide failed to reproduce it; readers on PubPeer found images reused from the lead author's own doctoral thesis; and genetic testing showed the 'STAP cells' were ordinary embryonic stem cells. Both papers were retracted in July 2014. Failed replication and duplicated images arriving at the same answer from two directions. T5c: the cost of being the person who checks — Bik has faced legal threats over her posts; more than 2,200 scientists signed in her support, and she was awarded the John Maddox Prize in 2021 for standing by evidence under pressure. T5d: the stubborn structural fact this ladder leaves the reader with — journals do not routinely screen images before publishing. Readers do it afterwards, unpaid.
source: Wikipedia 'Elisabeth Bik' (the 2013 plagiarism origin, the 2016 mBio screen of 20,621 papers with Casadevall and Fang, the 2019 Molecular and Cellular Biology analysis, PubPeer and Retraction Watch involvement, the Raoult legal threat and the 2,200-scientist petition, the 2021 John Maddox Prize); Wikipedia 'Sylvain Lesné' (the March 2006 Nature Aβ*56 paper, ~2,300 citations, Matthew Schrag's whistleblower report, Charles Piller's July 2022 Science investigation, the June 2024 retraction wording, and the split scientific response including Dennis Selkoe and the NIA statement); Wikipedia 'Haruko Obokata' (the January 2014 STAP Nature papers, worldwide replication failure, PubPeer/blogger image and thesis duplication findings, the genetic evidence that STAP cells were ordinary ES cells, RIKEN's April 2014 misconduct finding and the July 2014 retractions). PubPeer and Retraction Watch founding details flagged for build-time verification.
framing_note: Shape B CONCEPT ladder — the strand's analytic backbone and its bridge to the present day; the SPINE is the catch mechanism (the image as fingerprint, and replication), every rung a named case. RAIL (critical): Bik flags SUSPECTED duplication; findings of misconduct come from institutions afterwards — never write a rung saying she 'proved fraud'. RAIL (equally critical): T5 is mandatory — the Aβ*56 retraction did not refute the amyloid hypothesis, and a ladder that implies Alzheimer's research was all fake would itself be the failure mode this strand exists to teach against. TONE RAIL: do NOT use the death of STAP co-author Yoshiki Sasai as material. Optional extra rung ONLY if independently verified at build: the 2023 Stanford review of Marc Tessier-Lavigne's papers — and if used, state precisely that the panel did not find he personally manipulated data. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (speckles as a fingerprint) and T4b (the most-cited Alzheimer's paper, retracted). DISTRACTOR MINE: real integrity tools and real biology — western blots, gel electrophoresis, fluorescence microscopy, plagiarism-detection software, statistical forensics (GRIM, Benford), failed replication, preregistration — plus the real named investigators. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never let a stem mention 'the same photograph' before asking what Bik looks for.

name: The tell — what actually gives a faked result away
scope: CONCEPT ladder across four centuries-worth of cases: in every one, somebody did something concrete rather than deferring to somebody important. T2: INDIA INK — in the 1920s the Viennese biologist Paul Kammerer reported that midwife toads forced to breed in water had developed black, rough 'nuptial pads' and passed them to their offspring, which would have meant acquired characteristics are inherited. In 1926 G. K. Noble of the American Museum of Natural History examined the last surviving specimen and reported in Nature that the black patches were India ink, injected under the skin. T3: A FELT-TIP PEN — in March 1974 William Summerlin at Sloan-Kettering presented white mice bearing dark skin grafts supposedly accepted from unrelated donors, which would have been a transplant breakthrough. A laboratory assistant wiped one of the dark patches with alcohol and the colour came off. An inquiry led by C. Chester Stock found his conduct incompatible with science, and 'painting the mice' entered the language of research fraud. T4: NUMBERS TOO PERFECT — Leon Kamin noticed in the early 1970s that the British psychologist Cyril Burt's twin-study IQ correlations stayed identical to three decimal places even after new pairs of twins were added to the sample, which real data cannot do; in 1976 Oliver Gillie reported in the Sunday Times that Burt's named research assistants, Margaret Howard and J. Conway, could not be traced. T4b: THE HONEST-DISPUTE RUNG — the Burt case is still argued. His official biographer Leslie Hearnshaw concluded in 1979 that the post-war data were unreliable or invented; Robert Joynson (1989) and Ronald Fletcher (1991) argued the case against him was overstated; and later twin studies by other researchers found broadly similar heritability by independent means. The bank reports the dispute and declines to hand down a verdict it does not have. T5: ROWS SHIFTED BY ONE — from 2007 the statisticians Keith Baggerly and Kevin Coombes at MD Anderson tried to REPRODUCE Duke University's genomic predictors of which chemotherapy would work for a given cancer patient. Rebuilding the analysis from the raw files, they found gene lists shifted by one row and samples mislabelled. Duke had already opened clinical trials assigning real patients to treatments on that basis; the trials were suspended in 2010, eleven papers were retracted, and the final push came when The Cancer Letter found Anil Potti had claimed a Rhodes Scholarship he never held. T5b: THE THROUGH-LINE, the reason these four sit in one ladder — an ink stain under a microscope, an alcohol swab, a column of correlations added up by hand, and an analysis rebuilt from the raw files. Not one of them was an authority announcing the truth. Every one was somebody checking a physical thing.
source: Wikipedia 'Paul Kammerer' (the midwife toad nuptial-pad claim, G. K. Noble of the AMNH, the 1926 Nature report, the India-ink finding, Kammerer's response and death, and Koestler's later sabotage theory and its rejection); Wikipedia 'William Summerlin' (the March 1974 felt-tip-pen mice, the alcohol discovery by a research assistant, the C. Chester Stock committee finding, Robert Good's supervisory role, and 'painting the mice' as an idiom); Wikipedia 'Cyril Burt' (Kamin's identical-to-three-decimal-places finding, Gillie's 1976 Sunday Times report on Howard and Conway, the Hearnshaw 1979 biography, and the Joynson 1989 / Fletcher 1991 defences, with the dispute explicitly unresolved); Wikipedia 'Anil Potti' (the Duke genomic predictors, Baggerly and Coombes at MD Anderson from 2007, the three clinical trials suspended in 2010, The Cancer Letter's Rhodes Scholar finding, eleven retractions, and the 2012 IOM 'Evolution of Translational Omics' report). framing_note: Shape B CONCEPT ladder; the SPINE is the tell, and every rung is a named case with a physical act of checking at its centre — this is the strand's clearest statement of the bank's test-it-yourself soul. RAIL (non-negotiable): Cyril Burt is DISPUTED, not settled — the T4b rung must present both sides and reach no verdict, and no distractor may quietly assert 'proven fraud'. TONE RAIL: Kammerer died by suicide six weeks after Noble's paper; if the build mentions it at all, one clause, T4 or above, no method, no dwelling — the ladder's subject is the ink and the microscope. RAIL: Baggerly and Coombes reproduced an analysis; do not describe them as having caught a lie — they found errors, and the fraud finding came later. Dinner-test payoff: T3 — the alcohol swab that wiped the mouse clean. DISTRACTOR MINE: the graveyard of respectable-but-wrong real science these cases sat inside — Lamarckian inheritance of acquired characteristics (which is exactly what serious biologists were still weighing when Kammerer published), immune rejection and tissue matching, heritability and twin methodology, microarray gene-expression profiling — plus the real named checkers. No joke options. LANE: the ANIMAL bank owns the midwife toad's real natural history (the male carrying the egg strings wrapped round his hind legs); this rung keys the India ink and Noble's microscope, never the toad's biology.
